scenario.name: Sandworm HermeticWiper Signed EaseUS Driver (empntdrv.sys) MBR & NTFS $MFT Destruction
scenario.overview: Imagine a neighborhood auto repair garage with a wide roll-up shutter bay, a red rolling tool chest, spare tire racks, and a twin-post hydraulic car lift raising a sedan off the floor. Rolling a familiar customer sedan into the repair garage bay, a rogue mechanic hits the hydraulic switch to lift the car high above the concrete floor. In this real-world scenario, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the shop foreman's station, then smuggles copied records out past the garage roll-up service door in tiny disguised batches. During the next routine safety inspection, the shop foreman raises the sedan on the lift and spots the unrecorded aftermarket wire bolted beneath the frame. In this scenario (T1068, Sandworm HermeticWiper Signed EaseUS Driver (empntdrv.sys) MBR & NTFS $MFT Destruction), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: extracting, then disabling Volume Shadow Copy , Crash Dumps, then raw \\.\PhysicalDrive0..100 MBR. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Extracting, then Disabling Volume Shadow Copy , Crash Dumps, then Raw \\.\PhysicalDrive0..100 MBR, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 6 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Extracting & Registering Signed EaseUS Driver (empntdrv.sys) from RCDATA
stages.subtitle: Privilege Escalation & Defense Evasion (T1068 / T1543.003)
stages.description: Rolling a familiar customer sedan into the repair garage bay, a rogue mechanic hits the hydraulic switch to lift the car high above the concrete floor. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the shop foreman's station while everyday visitors and the shop foreman go about their routine. Upon execution via Active Directory GPO or WMI, HermeticWiper enabled SeLoadDriverPrivilege, SeBackupPrivilege, and SeShutdownPrivilege in its process token, checked the OS architecture and Windows version, decompressed an MSZIP-compressed resource (DRV_X64 / DRV_XP_X64) from its PE RCDATA section into C:\Windows\System32\drivers\<2_random_chars>dr.sys (a legitimate, Microsoft-signed copy of empntdrv.sys from EaseUS Partition Master), and loaded it into the kernel. Both the outer HermeticWiper executable (signed by Hermetica Digital Ltd until revoked) and the inner empntdrv.sys kernel driver (signed by CHENGDU YIWO Tech Development Co., Ltd.) carried valid Authenticode signatures at the time of the attack. Mechanically, this stage is complete only after [object Object] and [object Object] is observed as live runtime state (the concrete checkpoint proving the previous stage's output now drives the next action). stages.title: Stage 2: Disabling Volume Shadow Copy (vss), Crash Dumps & Fragmenting NTFS Metadata
stages.subtitle: Inhibit System Recovery & Defense Evasion (T1490 / T1070)
stages.description: Working underneath the raised chassis out of sight of the front waiting counter, the mechanic bolts a hidden bypass module directly onto the car’s starter wiring. Here in Step 2 inside the repair garage, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the shop foreman's station without disturbing the factory sealed spare-parts rack. HermeticWiper called ChangeServiceConfigW and ControlService to disable and stop the vss (Volume Shadow Copy) service, set HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\CrashControl\CrashDumpEnabled = 0 (preventing Windows from writing a MEMORY.DMP kernel crash dump when the corrupted system inevitably blue-screened, thereby denying incident responders RAM forensics), and parsed the raw NTFS boot sector and Master File Table ($MFT) to map the exact physical disk runlists of $MFT, $LogFile, $Bitmap, and C:\Windows\System32\config registry hives. By parsing the NTFS $MFT runlist fragments directly rather than using standard Windows file APIs, HermeticWiper could corrupt the exact physical sectors backing critical OS metadata even while Windows held those files locked. In the documented EventID 7040 exchange from Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap to HermeticWiper (conhost.dll / Hermetica), HermeticWiper (conhost.dll / Hermetica) responds with ALERT 7040 (confirming that the Stage 2: Disabling Volume Shadow Copy (vss), Crash Dumps & Fragmenting NTFS Metadata request succeeded on HermeticWiper (conhost.dll / Hermetica) and establishing the runtime state required for Step #3 Stage 3: Raw \.PhysicalDrive0..100 MBR & NTFS $MFT Overwrite with CSPRNG Bytes). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ Stage 2: Disabling Volume Shadow Copy (vss), Crash Dumps & Fragmenting NTFS Metadata / ⇠#2 ALERT 7040) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 HermeticWiper (conhost.dll / Hermetica)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 PhysicalDrive0 MBR & NTFS $MFT Wiped).

stages.title: Stage 3: Raw \\.\PhysicalDrive0..100 MBR & NTFS $MFT Overwrite with CSPRNG Bytes
stages.subtitle: Impact (T1561.002 - Disk Structure Wipe)
stages.description: Lowered back onto its wheels and washed spotless outside, the sedan drives off the garage lot carrying a hidden ignition backdoor that activates on every future start. In this final step inside the repair garage, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the garage roll-up service door in tiny disguised batches until the garage service checklist board catches the mismatch. Iterating through \\.\PhysicalDrive0 up to \\.\PhysicalDrive100, HermeticWiper generated cryptographically random bytes via CryptGenRandom and overwrote the Master Boot Record (MBR) (first 512 bytes of sector 0), GPT partition headers, and the mapped physical sector extents of $MFT, $LogFile, and C:\Users, before invoking ExitWindowsEx(EWX_REBOOT | EWX_FORCE) to immediately reboot the machine into an unrecoverable, unbootable state. Because the $MFT (which maps where every file resides on an NTFS volume) and $MFTMirr are overwritten with random bytes from CryptGenRandom, carving or recovering filesystem structure is rendered impossible in seconds without having to overwrite every gigabyte of the disk. Mechanically, this stage is complete only after [object Object] and [object Object] is observed as live runtime state (the concrete checkpoint proving the previous stage's output now drives the next action). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ Stage 3: Raw \\.\PhysicalDrive0..100 MBR & NTFS $MFT Overwrite with CSPRNG Bytes / ⇠#3 ALERT T1561.002) from Node ③ (#3 HermeticWiper (conhost.dll / Hermetica)) to Node ④ (#4 Signed EaseUS Driver (empntdrv.sys)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 PhysicalDrive0 MBR & NTFS $MFT Wiped).
